artworks.title: Old Tree Trunk
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image is a detailed sketch of a tree trunk showcasing the textured bark and knotted areas where branches may have grown. The drawing is centered vertically on the page, with the trunk extending upward. There is no visible horizon, emphasizing the tree itself. The pencil strokes emphasize the bark's rough texture and details. The color palette is neutral, with graphite on beige or light tan paper. Subtle hints of grass and uneven ground are suggested near the tree's base through shading and line work.

artworks.title: Tree
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image shows a view from below of a tall tree dominating the scene. The horizon is not visible. The pencil strokes capture the textures of the tree's bark and leaves. The color palette is shades of gray pencil on sepia-toned paper. The drawing features the tree's thick trunk, branches, and detailed twigs, with a soft and classic appearance. The background is undefined, emphasizing the detailed rendering of the tree.

artworks.title: A Glade of Trees
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with two trees in the foreground. One tree is taller and more detailed, with twisting branches reaching into the sky. The horizon is undefined, with land leveling gradually and less detailed trees and foliage in the distance. The brushstrokes are sketch-like, adding a soft texture to the leaves and bark, blending smoothly. The color scheme is monochromatic with shades of black, gray, and white, creating a serene atmosphere and emphasizing the details in the drawing.

artworks.title: The Hall, Levens, Westmorland
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: This is a painting of an elaborately decorated interior room. The image showcases a grand room with high ceilings, adorned with intricate stucco work and paneling. The walls are covered in richly carved wooden panels, and there is a red carpet on the floor, along with various pieces of ornate furniture, including red and gold-upholstered chairs. The room is illuminated by natural light coming through a window in the background. The setting conveys grandeur and historical significance, with an air of refined luxury typical of a past era.

artworks.title: The Dining Room, Levens, Westmorland
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: The image features three people seated at a round table in a lavishly decorated room. Each person is visible from the waist up. The person on the left has shoulder-length dark hair and wears a dark coat, facing the person on the right. The central person has dark hair and wears a dark dress with light-colored wrist area. The person on the right also has shoulder-length dark hair, dressed in a blue coat with white shirt and trousers, slightly reclined in the chair. The room has a red carpet, wood paneling, decorative ceiling molding, large windows with red drapery, a grand fireplace with a burning fire, red chairs along the walls, and dogs or figures of dogs on the floor. The room's ambiance is luxurious, with detailed patterns on the ceiling and woodwork.

artworks.title: Studies of Men and Boys
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image depicts a pencil sketch with various figures and objects. In the upper left corner, there is a full-body drawing of a nude person seated on a chair. On the right, there is a faint sketch of a man wearing a hat and coat, holding a pipe. Lower on the right, two clothed figures are drawn. One is an older man standing with a cane, and the other is a younger man. Below them is a sketch of a boot or shoe on a box or ledge. The background is plain with aged paper.

artworks.title: The Drawing Room, Levens, Westmorland
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: This is a painting of a room in a grand house or palace. The interior features wood paneling and a detailed ceiling decoration. A large fireplace is visible with a fire burning. Various pieces of elaborately carved furniture, including chairs and tables, are present, adorned with deep-hued upholstery. Additional decor, such as vases and a framed portrait, enhance the opulence. Light filters in through leaded glass windows, creating patterns on the walls. The style is classical architecture and interior detail.

artworks.title: Brereton, Cheshire
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: The image depicts a grand historic building with two towers. The structure has elaborate architectural details, including an arched entrance and intricately designed stonework. In the foreground, there is a path leading up to the building's entrance, flanked by greenery. Shadows and detailing create depth, while the blue sky above is filled with soft clouds. The style resembles that of Samuel Prout.

artworks.title: Pastoral Landscape
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with a pastoral scene, including trees, fields, and figures walking along a path. The horizon line is above the center of the image. The sketch features soft brushstrokes and a monochromatic color palette of gray on a tan-brown background.

artworks.title: Two Women
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image features two drawings of women shown from the shoulders up, facing the viewer. They appear to be seated upright. The woman on the left has hair styled with a center part and is secured behind her ears, cascading down the sides of her face. She has a composed expression and is adorned with earrings. She is wearing a garment with a high collar and ruffled layers around her shoulders. The woman on the right also has hair parted in the middle, falling just below her ears, with a calm expression. She wears a dress with a decorative neckline and a cross pendant around her neck. Both drawings are sketched in pencil on a sheet of muted beige paper, which is worn at the edges and corners. The background is plain and unadorned, consisting solely of the textured surface of the paper.

artworks.title: Small Drawing Room, Levens, Westmorland
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: The image shows a drawing room with a large ornately carved wooden fireplace at the center. The ceiling has an intricate geometric pattern and the color scheme consists of earthy browns, deep reds, and touches of green. On the left, there is a window with diamond-patterned glass, a red couch, and a table with a mandolin and sheet music. On the right, a lady in a light-colored dress is seated on a green couch reading, next to a dark wooden chest of drawers. A large portrait hangs on the wall above her, and two tall candlestands are placed near the dark open doorway on the right.

artworks.title: Banqueting Room, Bramhall, Cheshire
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: This is a painting of a banqueting room. The scene features a hall with a vaulted ceiling, wooden beams with carvings, heraldic decorations, mounted antlers, stained glass windows, a large table with benches, shields, a suit of armor, and a grand chair against a painted wall. The style resembles Victorian artist James Stephanoff's historical depictions of grand mansion halls.

artworks.title: Castle and Figures
artworks.medium: pen and black ink, wash, and graphite on wove paper mounted to wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image depicts an elevated perspective looking down at a castle-like structure with a tall steeple. The terrain slopes gently upward towards the horizon, merging with distant hills or mountains. The brushstrokes are detailed, adding texture to trees and buildings. Figures are seen engaging in activity, providing scale. The color palette consists of muted sepia tones, emphasizing architectural elements with variations in light and shadow.

artworks.title: The Old Corcoran Gallery of Art
artworks.medium: gouache over graphite on paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1951)
artworks.description: The illustration depicts a grand architectural building in black-and-white. The building is shown in intricate detail with columns, statues, and decorations. Trees and people can be seen in the surroundings. The sky is depicted with broad strokes, adding atmosphere to the scene. Other structures are faintly visible in the background.

artworks.title: Le groom public
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a coachman interacting with a passenger in a horse-drawn carriage. The drawing features a detailed scene of the individual guiding horses while engaging in conversation or actions related to the carriage. The artwork depicts intricate detailing of the carriage wheels, horses, and other elements, emphasizing movement and interaction between figures and objects. The style of the drawing focuses on line and form.

artworks.title: Study for "View of Mt. Washington"
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. and Mrs. John C. Newington, 1977)
artworks.description: The image is a pencil drawing of a landscape featuring a distant range of mountains. The drawing shows a view overlooking a broad expanse of land leading to the mountains, with the horizon placed towards the upper third of the image. The mountain peaks create a wavy line against the sky. The pencil strokes are delicate and light, showing details of trees and slopes without heavy shading. Close to the viewer, faint outlines indicate rolling hills and clusters of trees. The overall color palette is monochromatic due to the pencil medium. The background mountainous area contrasts with the sparse and open setting in the foreground.

artworks.title: Study for "Jephthah's Daughter"
artworks.medium: pen and black ink on blue wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1950)
artworks.description: The image shows abstract lines forming two figures. One figure reaches upward while the other leans against them. The background is a textured blue surface with small, evenly spaced specks. The figures' flowing lines suggest movement. The composition conveys dynamic grace and is connected to the expressive motions of dance.

artworks.title: Female Nude
artworks.medium: pastel on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image is a drawing of a nude female figure in a standing pose. The woman is depicted in profile, with her arms raised above her head. She has short, wavy reddish-brown hair and delicate facial features. The drawing emphasizes the contours of the human body using soft colors and shading. The background is a plain, textured surface.

artworks.title: Blacksmith in the Goldfields
artworks.medium: black ink wash over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1950)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a blacksmith working outdoors. The scene depicts a blacksmith holding a hammer over an anvil, creating sparks as he works on a piece of metal. Beside him, a person is sitting with a pickaxe, while another person is mounted on a horse. The background shows mountainous terrain with other figures climbing the slopes, carrying tools, suggesting a mountainous or mining setting. The drawing uses monochrome shades, capturing the rustic atmosphere of the scene with detailed attention to the texture of the rocks, the build of the working figures, and the movement of the horse.

artworks.title: The Scalp-Dance of the Sioux
artworks.medium: brown ink wash and graphite with scratched highlights on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1963)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of dancers performing a traditional dance. The drawing, done in sepia tones, depicts figures engaged in a dance. They are shown in mid-motion, wielding weapons and adorned with feathered headdresses and traditional attire. The background features teepees and a hazy atmosphere. The composition and style emphasize movement and cultural expression, capturing the intensity and rhythm of the dance.

artworks.title: Female Nude
artworks.medium: charcoal and white pastel on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image shows a full-body drawing of a person in a standing position. The person is depicted in profile, with their left arm extended outward and an upright posture. Facial features include an elongated nose and closed lips, with medium-length hair covering part of the neck. The drawing emphasizes textures and shapes using light and shadow to highlight form and contour. The figure is drawn on brown paper, creating a warm and neutral backdrop. There are no clothes or distinct background elements in the image, enhancing the focus on the figure.

artworks.title: Seated Female Nude
artworks.medium: charcoal and chalk on gray laid paper mounted to paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image is a drawing of a person seated on the floor in a relaxed pose. The person is unclothed with short, soft wavy hair and a necklace around their neck. They are sitting with legs extended and slightly bent, one arm behind supporting their weight, and the other arm resting on one knee. The face is turned to the side with a calm expression. The background is a plain, textured canvas.

artworks.title: Female Nude from Behind
artworks.medium: charcoal and chalk on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image shows a person's body in a dynamic pose, with one leg raised and bent at the knee and the other leg extended. The individual is captured mid-motion, with their upper body slightly leaning forward and one arm extended outward. The person has curly hair and their facial features are delicately outlined. The person appears nude and is not wearing any clothing or jewelry, and is not holding any objects. The background is a plain, textured surface of warm brown color.

artworks.title: The Quest
artworks.medium: charcoal and chalk on brown laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image is a drawing of a nude person in motion. The figure is shown with one arm raised, the other crossed over their chest, and one leg extended forward as if leaping or lunging. The face is in profile with defined features, and the hair appears curly or wavy. The figure is depicted with white and black accents for shading. The background is plain brown.
